# Edward Shen

> Engineering case studies on Go backends, distributed scheduling, data platforms, and lifecycle audience pipelines.

These articles describe project decisions, production observations, and implementation limits. Proposed changes are identified in the articles.

## Author

- [About Edward Shen](https://edwardshen125.github.io/about/): Career background and systems owned.

## Engineering case studies

- [Designing a Predicate-Driven Audience Pipeline for Lifecycle Email](https://edwardshen125.github.io/posts/engineering-case-study/building-a-predicate-driven-audience-pipeline-for-lifecycle-email/): How reusable predicates, AST compilation, and layered TiDB data let lifecycle campaigns combine user traits, events, and expiring assets into email audiences.
- [Building a Real-Time Data Platform With TiDB CDC and Flink](https://edwardshen125.github.io/posts/engineering-case-study/building-a-real-time-data-platform-with-tidb-cdc-and-flink/): How a four-engineer backend team built a TiCDC, Kafka, and Flink data platform on TiDB for second-level analytics, reconciliation, and QueryHub dashboards.
- [Scaling Four Engineers to Eighteen Go Services With Generated Contracts](https://edwardshen125.github.io/posts/engineering-case-study/scaling-four-engineers-to-eighteen-go-services-with-generated-contracts/): How four Go engineers used a shared API DSL, code generation, and platform defaults to deliver eighteen production services while controlling contract drift.
- [Debugging a Sporadic Go OOM in a Recursive JSON Encode Path](https://edwardshen125.github.io/posts/engineering-case-study/debugging-a-sporadic-go-oom-in-a-recursive-json-encode-path/): A Go service reached its 8 GB Pod memory limit when a recursive event type entered jsoniter's lazy encoder compilation path during publish. Build bisection isolated the type and publish path; moving only that path to sonic stopped the incident.
- [Building a Production Go Scheduler for 200K+ Delayed Jobs per Second](https://edwardshen125.github.io/posts/engineering-case-study/building-a-production-go-scheduler-for-200k-delayed-jobs-per-second/): How a Go scheduling center used TiDB, etcd, and Pulsar to publish more than 200K delayed jobs per second, and how production incidents reshaped its isolation model.
- [Running a Million-DAU Casual Game on Go: Rooms as the Concurrency Boundary](https://edwardshen125.github.io/posts/engineering-case-study/running-a-million-dau-casual-game-on-go-rooms-as-the-concurrency-boundary/): The room service of a QQ-licensed casual game with a million daily users, sized for tens of millions: one Go binary running room goroutines under Go's multicore scheduler, with a serial tick-driven ECS (entity–component–system) inside each room. How the concurrency boundary was chosen, and the pprof finding that moved component data from maps to pre-allocated arrays.
